transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sara Kim (Redwood AE), Jonas Patel (Redwood SE), Michael Reyes (Everleaf - Head Procurement), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Everleaf CTO), Priya Malhotra (Everleaf Legal)

Summary: Procurement/legal review of MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing approvals and onboarding. Focus on SOC2, KMS, SAML/SSO, SLA P95/P99 latency targets, and committed capacity pricing.

[00:00] Sara Kim: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, uh I'm Sara from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Jonas is our solutions engineer, he'll jump in on the technical bits. Michael, Dr. Lena, Priya, thanks for joining.
[00:08] Michael Reyes: Thanks Sara, yeah we wanted to run through the legal redlines and get a sense of the SLA commitments and pricing options before we push this to procurement.
[00:15] Jonas Patel: Hi all, quick wave. I'll cover the infra, SOC2, KMS, and how private deployments work, and then we can talk about latency SLAs and fallback policies.
[00:24] Priya Malhotra: Thanks. From Legal side I'll mostly be looking at the DPA clauses around data residency, breach notification timelines, and indemnity. We sent a first pass of redlines earlier this week.
[00:33] Sara Kim: Got it, we have your redlines, thanks. We can provide a redline-friendly MSA/DPA-- we usually send a copy with inline comments to make procurement easier.
[00:40] Dr. Lena Ortiz: On the technical front we need to confirm KMS support — customer-managed keys — and also whether you support VPC-only private control plane or an on-prem option for air-gapped workloads.
[00:52] Jonas Patel: Yep, we support customer-managed KMS via common providers and HSM integrations; we also offer a Private deployment model with VPC peering and an on-prem option for sensitive workloads. There are a few operational tradeoffs, e.g. telemetry and console access are via the private control plane, but we can toggle what we collect for compliance.
[01:10] Michael Reyes: Great. On SLAs: Procurement wants uptime and latency commitments. What do you typically commit to for Dedicated customers?
[01:18] Sara Kim: For Dedicated capacity we offer SLA-backed uptime (we can discuss 99.9% vs 99.95% for enterprise tiers) and latency SLOs are typically defined in the contract as P95/P99 response times for specific model classes and sequence lengths.
[01:30] Jonas Patel: To add, latencies vary by model and seq length — we usually specify p95 for 512-token inferenced with model X variant on our dedicated instances. We can include measured baselines from our redwood-verified performance profiles.
[01:44] Priya Malhotra: How are credits/penalties structured if you miss the SLA?
[01:48] Sara Kim: Standard remedy is service credits tied to downtime windows; for latency breaches we typically have a remediation plan and credits if sustained operational regressions occur. We'll map to specific thresholds in the MSA appendix.
[02:02] Dr. Lena Ortiz: We also care about performance regressions after model changes. Do you provide quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to our eval sets?
[02:09] Jonas Patel: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring; we can wire up your eval prompt set for regression detection and alerting. That can be included as an addendum or ops SLA.
[02:18] Michael Reyes: Pricing — we need committed capacity pricing vs pay-as-you-go. Procurement wants committed monthly commit with a discount and burst on top. Can you outline that?
[02:27] Sara Kim: Absolutely. We'll share the pricing worksheet: options for Hosted (usage-based) and Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) with monthly commit discounts. Bursting and autoscaling policies can be added as well. I'll send the detailed numbers after the call.
[02:38] Michael Reyes: Cool. Any competitor differences we should be mindful of? The CTO asked about comparisons to Anthropic and OpenAI on cost and VPC options.
[02:46] Jonas Patel: Quick take: many public APIs don't offer private on-prem or VPC deployment with the same operational tooling. Redwood's diff is the unified runtime across hosted and private with routing/fallbacks, and more prescriptive batching/quantization controls to reduce unit cost.
[03:02] Priya Malhotra: On data handling — where does user data live and how long is it retained? We need clear DPA terms for retention and deletion, and audit logs for access.
[03:11] Sara Kim: For Hosted, default retention is minimal and we can commit to contract-level retention windows; Dedicated and Private give you full control — logs can be routed to your SIEM and retention adheres to your policy. We'll include the DPA language and our standard audit log descriptions.
[03:26] Dr. Lena Ortiz: For our pilot, we plan to run a constrained workload: 200 qps at peak, mix of chat and embeddings. We need target 95th percentile generation latency under 300ms for short chat turns, ideally. Is that realistic?
[03:38] Jonas Patel: For short chat (<=128 tokens) on dedicated optimized nodes, p95 under 300ms is achievable depending on model and quantization. We'll propose a model variant and config in the performance appendix; we'll also run a benchmark during the pilot.
[03:52] Michael Reyes: What about keys and audits — Priya needs to see SOC2 Type II and maybe penetration test summaries.
[03:58] Sara Kim: We can provide SOC2 Type II report, pen test summary, and an architecture diagram. Jonas will drop those artifacts.
[04:06] Jonas Patel: I'll share the infra diagram, SOC2, and the KMS/SAML integration notes. Also, a small note: if you opt for Private on-prem deployment, the onboarding calendar is longer — usually 6–8 weeks for air-gapped installs.
[04:20] Priya Malhotra: That timeline is fine as long as we align procurement. Also, we have standard contract redlines around indemnity and liability caps — expect more questions there.
[04:29] Sara Kim: Understood — we'll send a redline-friendly copy and highlight the sections to expedite review. If helpful we can offer a legal-to-legal touchpoint.
[04:37] Michael Reyes: Good — last, can you confirm where pricing approvals sit? Our procurement needs a committed quote to present to finance.
[04:44] Sara Kim: I'll send a committed quote and pricing worksheet with the two recommended options: a 12-month reserved capacity (discounted) and a 3-month pilot with defined burst. That will include PO and invoicing terms.
[04:55] Dr. Lena Ortiz: On telemetry — we need control over what telemetry you collect in Private mode; can that be fully disabled?
[05:02] Jonas Patel: In Private mode telemetry is configurable — we can limit it to essential health metrics for SLA verification and expose logs to your SIEM. For on-prem truly air-gapped installs, telemetry can be disabled; documentation will be included.
[05:14] Michael Reyes: Okay that covers most of our asks. Next steps?
[05:18] Sara Kim: Recap: I'll send the MSA/DPA redline-friendly copies, the pricing worksheet, and the quote by Thursday (2026-03-26). Jonas will share SOC2, infra diagram, and KMS/SAML notes by Wednesday (2026-03-27). You (Michael) will confirm procurement timeline and PO process by end of next week. We'll aim to schedule a follow-up week of 2026-04-06 to finalize SLAs and kick off pilot.
[05:40] Priya Malhotra: Sounds good. Please include a summary of SLA remedies in the appendix so legal can review quickly.
[05:46] Sara Kim: Will do. Anything else?
[05:49] Dr. Lena Ortiz: No, thanks — looking forward to the benchmark data.
[05:52] Michael Reyes: Thanks everyone.
[05:54] Sara Kim: Thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.

Notes: Transcript occasionally has auto-caption errors; speaker attribution may be slightly off in a few lines. References to specific model names redwood-verified profiles are intentionally generic; exact model variant and perf appendix will be attached to the contract package.
